newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Senate OKs loan allowing Banerj selloff.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Senate OKs loan allowing Banerj selloff.

text.p: The Brazilian Senate on Tuesday approved a federal loan to Rio de Janeiro state, clearing the way for the privatization of state bank Banerj, congressional officials said.
Senators voted 43-10, with three abstentions, to approve the deal following the loan's endorsement only hours before by a Senate panel.

The 3.09 billion reais loan from mortgage bank Caixa Economica Federal (CEF) will be used to cover Banerj's pension and payroll-related debts, which was seen as key to make the bank appealing to investors.
Banerj, the first of Brazilian state-owned banks due to be privatized, had been scheduled to be sold off last week, but the auction was put on hold pending the Senate vote.
Four banks -- Bradesco, BCN, Banco Itau and Cia. de Investimentos Latino-Americana, represented by local Banco Pactual -- have presented financial guarantees to bid at the auction.

The Rio state bank, formally known as Banco Banerj S.A., will be sold for at least 310 million reais, down from an asking price of 480 million reais last year when previous attempts to sell the bank were held up by legal challenges and debt concerns.
